subject: Scheduling — ACME latency results demo & security handoff
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@acme-net.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Scheduling — ACME latency results demo & security handoff

Hi Ravi —

Thanks again for running the initial throughput tests last week. We'd like to schedule a 45-minute readout where our SE team walks through the token-level latency numbers, key tradeoffs, and the small set of artifacts your security team requested. Proposed agenda (high-level):

- 10m: quick recap and success criteria
- 25m: latency results & KV/cache behavior (Diego)
- 5m: outstanding questions and next steps
- 5m: procurement/contract checklist (Karthik / Marissa)

Can you share 2–3 45-min windows next week (Jan 18–22) in which you can join with your engineer(s) and a security point-of-contact? Also confirm who from your side should receive the security artifact package (SOC2 + network diagram + test harness logs).

I’ve attached the security questionnaire we usually start with and a short test-plan we’ll reference. If you prefer, we can make the session 60 minutes to allow a live replay of a short trace.

Thanks,
Stephanie

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai
[Attachment: ACME_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: redwood-latency-test-plan.md (md)]

Stephanie — thanks, this looks good. Lisa (lead engineer) and I can do any of these slots:

- Mon Jan 18: 10:00–10:45 PT
- Tue Jan 19: 13:00–13:45 PT
- Wed Jan 20: 09:30–10:15 PT

SecOps (secops@acme-net.com) wants the SOC2 and a short network diagram prior to the meeting — they asked for evidence that the test environment was isolated and no customer data left the cluster. Procurement looped in for PO timing — procurement@acme-net.com will confirm if they need a draft SOW beforehand.

Prefer Tue 13:00 if that works for you.

—Ravi

Sounds good — Tuesday 13:00 PT tentatively blocked on our side. Marissa, can you join briefly for procurement and next-step items? Karthik — can you surface any contract timing constraints (SOW/PO) that could affect a Jan 31 target?

Diego — for the demo please be prepared to:
- show token-level percentile graphs for long/short queries
- explain prefix/KV caching behavior and an example trace
- confirm the exact hardware used for the runs and the quantization profile

Ravi/Lisa — security wants the SOC2 PDF and a one-page network diagram. We can provide a redacted logs bundle for the demo. Does secops@acme-net.com prefer the files via SFTP or a secure share link?

If Tuesday is final I'll send the calendar invite and attach the final agenda (short).

Thanks,
Stephanie

Thanks — I’ll take the demo. Quick checklist from the SE side so we don’t waste time:

- I need the sample workload you ran (query set + sample inputs) — please upload to the shared doc (link below) or SFTP.
- I’ll prepare a short replay (5–7 mins) of a 99th percentile trace and a 95/99/99.9 table.
- I’ll include the hardware manifest (GPU type, kernel versions) and the quantization profile we used.
- If you want a live tracer, we’ll need a test user that can trigger the workload from your side (one engineer in the call).

Attachment: redwood-latency-test-plan.md (contains commands and log collection steps).

—Diego

Hi team — SecOps here. A couple of clarifying asks before we confirm attendance: 

1) Please provide SOC2 Type II report (or customer redacted copy) and the one-page network diagram showing test isolation
2) A redacted sample of the trace/logs (no customer PII) — the log format and a short README are sufficient
3) Confirmation that the demo environment is in our account or isolated VPC (if hosted)

We are available Tue Jan 19 13:00–13:45 PT but would prefer Tue 16:00 PT as an alternative if logistics for the tracer are tight. We accept secure share links (Box/Drive with restricted access).

If you can get items 1–3 uploaded by end of day Monday (Jan 18), we’ll be able to attend and focus on the controls rather than the infra details.

—ACME SecOps
